NOTE 6. Special Ferry Flight Authorization. Flight Standards District Offices (FSDO) is authorized to issue Special overweight ferry flight authorizations. These airplanes are structurally satisfactory for ferry flight if maintained within the following limits:

Takeoff weight must not exceed 130% of the maximum weight for Normal Category.

The Never Exceed Airspeed (VNE) and Maximum Structural Cruising Speed (VC) must be reduced by 30%.

Forward and aft center of gravity limits may not be exceeded.

Structural load factors of +2.5 g. to -1.0 g. may not be exceeded.

Requirements for any additional oil should established in accordance with AC 23.1011-1. Increased stall speeds and reduced climb performance should be expected for the increased weights. Flight characteristics and performance at the increased weights have not been evaluated. Flight Permit for operations of overweight aircraft may be found in AC 21-4B.

S/N 17280001 and On The certificated empty weight and corresponding center of gravity location must include unusable fuel of 18 lb. at 46.0 inches aft of datum, and full oil of 15.0 lb. at 13.1 inches forward of datum.

NOTE 2: The airplane must be operated according to the appropriate Pilot's Operating Handbook and FAA Approved Airplane Flight Manual (POH/AFM). POH/AFM P/N 172RPHUS00, or later FAA approved revision, is applicable to Production Model 172R. POH/AFM P/N 172R180PH00, or later FAA approved revision, is applicable to Production Model 172R airplanes when modified by Cessna Modification Kit MK172-72-01. All POH/AFM Supplements approved for P/N number 172RPHUS00, are also applicable to P/N 172R180PH00, unless specifically noted otherwise in the Supplement. All FAA required placards are included in Section 2 of the applicable POH/AFM, the applicable operating rules, or the certification basis must be installed as specified via the parts list for 0500530, Airplane Assembly (useful placarding reference is the Textron Aviation Illustrated Parts Catalogue (IPC). Any discrepancies identified between the IPC and an aircraft under inspection need to be reconciled using the previously stated parts list).

FAA Approved AFM: P/N 172RPHAUS-00, or later FAA approved revision, is applicable to the Model 172R equipped with Garmin G1000 Integrated Cockpit System. The airplane must be operated according to the appropriate AFM. Required placards are included in the AFM, the applicable operating rules, or the certification basis must be installed as specified via the parts list for 0500530, Airplane Assembly (useful placarding reference is the Textron Aviation IPC. Any discrepancies identified between the IPC and an aircraft under inspection need to be reconciled using the previously stated parts list).

FAA Approved AFM: P/N 172RPHBUS-00, or later FAA approved revision, are applicable to the Model 172R equipped with Garmin G1000 Integrated Cockpit System and Garmin GFC-700 AFCS. The airplane must be operated according to the appropriate AFM. Required placards are included in the AFM, the applicable operating rules, or the certification basis must be installed as specified via the parts list for 0500530, Airplane Assembly (useful placarding reference is the Textron Aviation IPC. Any discrepancies identified between the IPC and an aircraft under inspection need to be reconciled using the previously stated parts list).

NOTE 3: Special Ferry Flight Authorization. FSDO is authorized to issue special overweight ferry flight authorizations. This airplane is structurally satisfactory for ferry flight if maintained within the following limits:

Takeoff weight must not exceed 130% of the maximum weight for Normal Category.

The Never Exceed Airspeed (VNE) and Maximum Structural Cruising Speed (VC) must be reduced by 30%.

Forward and aft center of gravity limits may not be exceeded.

Structural load factors of +2.5 g. to -1.0 g. may not be exceeded.

Requirements for any additional oil should be established in accordance with AC 23.1011-1. Increased stall speeds and reduced climb performance should be expected for the increased weights. Flight characteristics and performance at the increased weights have not been evaluated. Flight Permit for operations of overweight aircraft may be found in AC 21-4B.

Airworthiness directives at Anfa
New mechanics, first month Quality: Karim Bennani
Speaker notes: This deck is for mechanics in their first month. It covers how we decide whether a directive applies and how we record it. Ask the quality manager about anything it does not cover.

Where directives come from
The state of design issues them: the FAA for our Cessnas Published in the Federal Register Revisions and corrections follow
Speaker notes: Corrections are published as separate notices, sometimes weeks later. A correction can change the applicability or a compliance time. AD 2020-16-08 on the Aspen displays is an example: read the rule and its correction together.

Check applicability before you sign
Model and serial number range Installed equipment and part number Software version, modifications
Speaker notes: Two traps in our own fleet. CN-TFC is a 172S like CN-TFA and CN-TFB, but its serial number is above the range of AD 2013-11-11. CN-TFD has a KAP 140 autopilot, but its serial number is outside the range of the KAP 140 directives. Equipment alone is not enough, and serial numbers alone are not enough.

The engine oil pressure switch
P/N 83278, 3,000 hours Replace with a new, zero-time switch Record part number, date, and airframe hours
Speaker notes: The 50-hour allowance in paragraph (g)(6) of AD 2013-11-11 applied once, to switches that were already at or near the limit when the directive took effect on 1 August 2013. It is not a grace period you can use today. Our manual, section 3.2, applies the same 3,000-hour limit to every 172R and 172S we maintain.

Torque
Maintenance manual first AC 43.13-1B Table 7-1 when it gives no value Record the wrench number
Speaker notes: Read the notes printed with Table 7-1 before you use it: they limit when its values apply. If a value looks wrong, stop and ask; do not guess between two columns.

Records
14 CFR 43.9 content in every entry AD compliance record for each aircraft Hours to one decimal place
Speaker notes: Check every number you copy. A swapped pair of digits in an installation time moves the next due time by 90 hours, and nobody notices until the records are audited.
